content: Healthcare providers are not required to report women seeking abortion-related care to law enforcement. Women must have access to emergency medical care, including post-abortion care, without fear of criminal penalties or reprisals. Requiring healthcare providers to report cases of abortion violates women’s right to privacy. Denial of therapeutic abortion may arbitrarily interfere with the right to privacy. Requiring third-party or judicial authorization for abortion violates the right to privacy, as it imposes unnecessary barriers and may lead to unsafe, illegal abortions. Criminalizing abortion is a violation of international human rights law and constitutes gender-based violence, which may amount to cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. Forced or coerced abortion is considered cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment and may constitute torture, particularly when conducted on women with disabilities. Conducting abortions on women with disabilities against their will, even under lawful decision-making processes by a legal guardian, can amount to torture or ill-treatment. Non-consensual abortion aimed at correcting or alleviating disability is a form of torture and ill-treatment. States must prohibit and prevent forced abortion, including in conflict settings, as it violates the right to decide on the number and spacing of children. Women, adolescents, and all individuals capable of becoming pregnant have the right to make informed, free, and responsible decisions about their reproduction, body, and SRH, free from discrimination, coercion, and violence. This right is rooted in bodily autonomy and self-determination. Women with disabilities have the right to control and make free decisions regarding their sexuality and SRH, free from coercion, discrimination, and violence. Health information must be provided in a manner that considers individual needs, including age, gender, language ability, education, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, and intersex status. All individuals and groups have the right to evidence-based information on SRH, including safe abortion and post-abortion care, in accessible formats.
